title: Backward sweep with leftward growth
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet and let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$ with $k>0$ work tapes. Choose $a_0\in\Gamma$, a state $q$, an input symbol (possibly blank), a read-symbol assignment for the work tapes, and a Boolean right-head flag for each tape. Suppose the action prescribed by $M$ has at least one tape whose right-head flag is true and whose head movement is left. For any input-head position, output word, integer frontier $z$, and left stack $l$, the augmented simulator, starting in the backward-writing phase with the boundary marker on its right, reaches after $k+2$ steps the configuration in the left-growth phase whose state is the action's successor state (if any). Its frontier is $z-k$, its left stack is the new leftward row—marked exactly on tapes with a right-head flag and a leftward move—followed by $l$, and its right stack remains the boundary marker; the work-tape head stays in $[z-k,z]$ throughout.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$

The transition action has a tape flagged on the right that moves left
An input-head position, output word, integer $z$, and left stack $l$
